title: Biceps brachii
source: OpenStax A&P 2e: 11.1 Interactions of Skeletal Muscles; 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs; 8.2; 14.3; 16.4

main.t: The two-headed muscle at the front of the arm that bends the elbow and turns the palm up.

simpler.t: The biceps is the muscle at the front of your upper arm that bends your elbow.

deeper.t: It crosses both the shoulder and the elbow, so it also helps flex the arm at the shoulder.

facts.t: It lies in the anterior compartment of the arm, with the brachialis deep to it.
Its two heads arise from the scapula: the coracoid process and the tubercle above the glenoid cavity.
Its tendon inserts on the radial tuberosity of the radius.
facts.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–17, 19–23 and 25). The insertion of the biceps brachii (radial tuberosity).

simpler.t: It runs down the front of your upper arm, from your shoulder blade to your forearm.

deeper.t: The tendon of the long head runs in the intertubercular (bicipital) groove of the humerus.

items.name: Long head
items.t: Arises above the glenoid cavity. Its tendon passes through the bicipital groove.

items.name: Short head
items.t: Arises from the coracoid process of the scapula.

items.name: Belly
items.t: The plump middle of the muscle. It bulges more as the muscle shortens.

items.name: Fusiform shape
items.t: A spindle-shaped belly that tapers towards each end.
items.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–17, 19–23 and 25). That the biceps brachii itself is fusiform (11.1 uses it as the example of a belly).

simpler.t: It has two heads at the top that join into one belly.

deeper.t: “Bi” in its name means it has two origins; “tri” in triceps means three.

facts.t: It flexes the forearm at the elbow, and supinates it at the radioulnar joints.
It is the prime mover in lifting a cup. The brachialis assists as a synergist.
The triceps brachii, at the back of the arm, is its antagonist.

simpler.t: It bends your elbow and turns your palm to face up.

items.name: Brachialis
items.t: Lies deep to the biceps and adds power to elbow flexion.

items.name: Triceps brachii
items.t: In the posterior compartment. It extends the forearm, opposing the biceps.

items.name: Brachioradialis
items.t: The third elbow flexor. It can flex the forearm quickly or help lift a load slowly.

items.name: Humerus
items.t: The long-head tendon runs in its intertubercular groove.

items.name: Musculocutaneous nerve
items.t: The nerve of the anterior compartment of the arm.
items.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–17, 19–23 and 25). The musculocutaneous nerve and its supply to the biceps.

simpler.t: It works with the brachialis and against the triceps.

facts.t: Like other limb muscles, it develops from general mesoderm. Spinal nerves then form its neuromuscular junctions.
Resistance training thickens its fibres by adding myofibrils (hypertrophy). No new fibres form.

items.injury: Damage to the lower motor neurons that supply the biceps.
items.damaged: The motor side of the biceps stretch reflex.
items.cannotDo: Show a normal biceps reflex when the tendon is tapped.
items.why: The reflex needs the spindle’s sensory fibre, the spinal synapse and the motor neuron intact.

items.injury: A heavy lift that ruptures the tendon of the long head.
items.damaged: The long-head tendon, where it runs in the bicipital groove.
items.cannotDo: Flex and supinate with full strength; the belly bunches up near the elbow.
items.why: The torn head cannot pull, and its belly shortens away from the tear.
items.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–17, 19–23 and 25). Rupture of the long head of the biceps and its signs.

items.q: Explain how the biceps and brachialis share the work of lifting a cup.
model: The biceps is the prime mover for the movement.
The brachialis, deep to it, assists as a synergist.
Both flex the forearm at the elbow.
The triceps relaxes as their antagonist.

items.q: Compare the biceps brachii and the brachialis.
model: The biceps crosses the shoulder and elbow; the brachialis arises from the distal humerus.
Only the biceps supinates the forearm.
The brachialis lies deep to the biceps.

items.q: Predict what happens to the triceps when the biceps contracts in a withdrawal reflex.
model: The sensory neuron excites an interneuron in the spinal cord.
The interneuron inhibits the triceps’ motor neuron.
The triceps relaxes instead of resisting.

check.stem: Which muscle is the antagonist of the biceps brachii at the elbow?
check.why: The triceps brachii extends the forearm, opposing the biceps.

check.stem: Besides flexing the elbow, what else does the biceps brachii do?
check.why: It also supinates the forearm at the radioulnar joints.

check.stem: Where does the short head of the biceps arise?
check.why: The short head arises from the coracoid process; the long head from the tubercle above the glenoid cavity.
